newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Two inmates killed in Albania jail breakout riot.
newsitem.headline: Two inmates killed in Albania jail breakout riot.

text.p: Two inmates were killed when prisoners rioted in an Albanian jail on Sunday after hearing about a wave of protests around the Balkan country, a top prison official said on Monday.
Inmates fought with wardens and police and set fire to cells at the Bardhor jail, near Kavaje, 50 km (30 miles) west of Tirana, said deputy director-general of prisons Bedri Coku.
"After they heard the main news, they tried to exploit the situation and wanted to break out of prison," he said.
"They were influenced by the recent events of vandalism and destruction all over the country," he added.
In demonstrations against crumbling pyramid savings schemes, protesters battled with riot police in the capital on Sunday and set buildings ablaze in at least four towns in the south.
Coku told a news conference in Tirana that inmates set fire to prison cells, destroying the dormitory block.
"Two prisoners died and three others were injured," he said. Two police officers were also hurt in the clash.
Police reinforcements were called in to break up the riot and the situation was now under control, he said.
Coku described the riot as the first prison revolt since Albania began its transition from communism to democracy in 1990.
Security in all Albania's jails had already been stepped up and Coku said prison authorities would not hesitate to call in the army if trouble got out of control.
On Sunday, Albania's parliament gave special powers to President Sali Berisha enabling him to deploy the military to guard strategic buildings and free roads blocked by protesters.
